conventions.convention: States, actions and observations are finite and nonempty; every action is available in every state. The next-state/reward law is joint, and observations depend only on the next state.
Policies observe past actions and observations but do not observe realized rewards. Their randomization depends only on that history and is conditionally independent of the hidden state.

Beliefs use the Borel sigma-algebra of the Euclidean simplex. The Bayes filter is defined only when the observation normalizer is positive; zero-normalizer branches are omitted from K without assigning a posterior.
Horizons are natural numbers including zero, and the discount lies in [0,1], including both endpoints.
The backup stores sets of vectors, removing duplicates, while policy trees retain their distinct root-action and observation-continuation descriptions.
A witness permits ties and may be any belief in the simplex; it need not be reachable from the specified initial belief.
Natural numbers are von Neumann naturals, include zero, and their strict additive order agrees with membership; I_n equals n and has cardinality n.

load_bearing.statement: A finite known-model POMDP specifies finite nonempty S, A and Ω, a joint next-state/reward probability mass p, next-state observation laws O, and an initial belief. Policies use only past actions and observations; realized rewards are excluded from history.

The belief is the conditional state distribution on a positive-probability observed-history atom. Prediction uses T; q is the observation marginal; τ is the prior-weighted observation likelihood divided by q when q>0 and is undefined when q=0. K sums the positive-mass posterior point masses.

The joint next-state/reward/observation mass is normalized; the predicted state and observation laws are probability distributions; every defined posterior is the conditional next-state distribution; and K is a probability kernel from Δ(S)×A to Δ(S). No Axiom of Choice is used.

At every positive-probability history and positively selected action, the next-state/observation law and conditional expected reward depend only on the current belief and action. For every remaining finite horizon, V_0=0 and V_{n+1}(b)=max_a[bar r(b,a)+γ sum_{o:q>0}q(o|b,a)V_n(τ(b,a,o))]. Each maximum is attained, randomization cannot improve it, and no Axiom of Choice is used.

Starting with Γ_0={0}, form Γ_{h+1} from every action and every observation-indexed tuple of Γ_h vectors by α(s)=r(s,a)+γ sum_{s'}T(s'|s,a) sum_o O(o|s')α_o(s'); store equal vectors once and return Γ_0 through Γ_H.

For 0≤h≤H and every belief b, V_h(b)=max_{α∈Γ_h} sum_s b(s)α(s). The value is piecewise linear and convex; deleting all vectors without witness beliefs preserves it. Policy-tree counts satisfy N_0=1 and N_{h+1}=|A|N_h^{|Ω|}, bounding the candidate and witness-vector counts.
For each n∈N, let I_n={t∈N:t<n}. Then I_n=n, so I_n is finite and |I_n|=n.

published_dependencies.used_for: Von Neumann naturals, zero and successor conventions.
The additive natural-number order defining clock initial segments.
Identification of strict natural order with membership and the presence of zero in positive naturals.
Finite cardinalities, cardinality of a natural, and transport along bijections.
Pointwise probability sections and measurable event evaluations.
Choice-free posterior formula at positive finite marginal density, specialized to finite counting measure; its null-fibre filler is distinguished from the local partial filter.
Measurability of observation probabilities obtained by integration against the predicted-state probability kernel.
Enumeration-independent finite sums and bijective reindexing.
Interchange of finite sums in normalization and marginal calculations.
Linearity, scaling and monotonicity of finite sums.
Attained maxima of nonempty finite real value sets.
Natural-valued exponentiation in policy-tree and function-set counts.
Finiteness and cardinalities of finite Cartesian products.
Finiteness and cardinality of observation-indexed continuations and hidden binary strings.
Induction for backup representations, tree counts and clock progression.
Initial-segment reward sums and empty-sum conventions.
Natural successor and arithmetic conventions in the clock example.
Transitivity of the natural clock set in the clock-progression induction.

lem-nat-order-is-membership, Statement, includes “([[def-natural-numbers]])” before completing its hypotheses and “([[def-nat-order]])” before its conclusions. These inline links interrupt the complete statement and are not moved into Statement references.

def-finite-cardinality, Definition, includes “([[def-natural-numbers]])” and “membership in [[lem-nat-order-is-membership]]” within the defining exposition, with additional supplier links throughout that section. It lacks the required uninterrupted Definition followed by Definition references.

thm-product-rule, Statement, includes “([[def-finite-cardinality]])” in clause 1 and “[[def-nat-finite-sum-and-product]]” in clause 2. The complete statement must precede these hyperlinks in a separate Statement references section.

thm-cardinality-of-a-set-of-functions, Statement, says “the power being the ... exponentiation of [[def-nat-power]]” before its degenerate-case qualifications. The hyperlink interrupts the statement and has no following Statement references section.

def-finite-sum, Definition, opens with links including “([[def-complete-ordered-field]])” and “([[def-natural-numbers]])”, then contains further inline supplier links before completing its recurrence and endpoint conventions. These violate the uninterrupted-definition rule.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier page inventory and def-finite-markov-decision-process against def-finite-pomdp. The consumer faithfully specializes the supplier's possibly empty finite state set and state-dependent nonempty action sets to nonempty S and a common nonempty A. It preserves the joint next-state/reward law and its expected-reward and transition marginals, renaming P to T and adding next-state observations. It does not import a finite-state Bellman theorem for the continuous belief simplex; that recursion is proved locally.
